description: Francium is a chemical element with symbol Fr and atomic number 87. It is extremely radioactive with its most stable isotope francium-223 having a half-life of only 22 minutes. It is the second-most electropositive element behind caesium and classed as an alkali metal.
uses: Due to its extreme instability and rarity, francium has no commercial applications. It has been used for research purposes in chemistry and atomic structure, particularly in specialized spectroscopy experiments that have provided data on atomic energy levels. Its use as a potential diagnostic aid for various cancers has been explored but deemed impractical, and it is a prospective candidate for searching for CP violation.
characteristics: Francium is one of the most unstable naturally occurring elements and as an alkali metal with a single valence electron, its chemical properties mostly resemble those of caesium. Its estimated melting point is around 8–27 °C with an estimated boiling point of 620 °C, though these values are uncertain due to the element's extreme rarity and radioactivity. Its density is expected to be around 2.48 g/cm³ and it has an estimated electronegativity of 0.7 on the Pauling scale.
